PullRequest.Title: mcp: validate gallery server sources and package types
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- restrict direct MCP server-document requests to the configured gallery origin and server path before performing network I/O
- disable redirect following for those requests and make the shared fetch request path honor `followRedirects: 0`
- validate package registry types at runtime in both supported gallery schema families and in the Copilot NuGet manifest mapper
- fail closed before command construction while retaining supported packages or remote transports and skipping only unusable gallery entries

## Why

MCP install links can open server documents by URL. Previously, the request was issued before confirming that the URL belonged to the configured gallery, and a non-gallery response could be processed by the compatibility serializer. In addition, older manifest shapes carried `registryType` values through without runtime validation, while the command mapper treated unknown values as executable names.

This change establishes the gallery origin/path as the network boundary and ensures that only registry types with explicit launch implementations can reach command construction. Unsupported package formats no longer make otherwise usable servers or entire gallery pages disappear.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an MCP server install link containing a direct gallery server URL
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve the active gallery manifest, validate the URL, fetch one server document, parse it, then open the server UI. The manifest and server request are on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the individual MCP server document with redirects disabled
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for a valid direct install URL; zero for a URL rejected by origin/path validation. Redirect targets are no longer requested.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One initial server request was also made, with fetch redirects followed automatically; invalid external URLs could also trigger that request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request must complete before the server editor opens.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe supported gallery versions when a custom gallery omits an explicit version
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two probes on the cold custom-gallery path, coalesced by the manifest service's initPromise/versionByUrl caches; normally zero for the product gallery's fixed v0.1 version.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A valid direct URL fetched the server first and then resolved the same manifest; total boundary cardinality was unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The changed method now awaits manifest resolution before the server request, but the same manifest resolution already occurred later on the pre-diff valid-URL path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user-opened install URL; URL parsing and package filtering scale with one server document and its package count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The direct install path is serial. Manifest initialization is promise-coalesced; there is no new concurrent burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workbench manifest initialization is cached by initPromise, and custom-version discovery is cached by URL. Server documents are not cached before or after this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the direct caller, manifest cache, and request call were traced end to end.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Registry latency varies, but the diff does not add a request and prevents redirect/external requests on rejected inputs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Valid links retain the same required manifest and server boundaries, while rejected links and redirects perform less network work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Synchronize installed MCP servers with gallery metadata by name
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After a delayed registry sync, deduplicate installed servers by name, resolve the shared manifest once, and resolve each unique name through configured endpoints before applying metadata. This is asynchronous maintenance rather than an input/render critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each unique installed server through latest, named, and optional ID gallery endpoints
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to three sequential endpoint requests per unique server name; names run concurrently via Promise.all. Effective cardinality is the number of deduplicated installed server names.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same endpoints, ordering, and Promise.all fan-out existed. The diff passes the already-resolved manifest into getMcpServer and adds local URL validation before each unchanged request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of background registry synchronization, not immediate UI progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct installed MCP server names after Map deduplication, typically a small user-managed set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One serial endpoint chain per unique name, with all unique names concurrently active through the existing Promise.all; no limiter or new concurrency was introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: One cached/coalesced manifest is shared across the batch; individual server responses are uncached both before and after the change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: caller deduplication, shared manifest ownership, endpoint loop, and concurrency were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large installed-server sets could expose the pre-existing unbounded Promise.all fan-out, but the diff neither introduces nor amplifies it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added URL parsing is small local CPU work relative to unchanged network resolution, and redirect suppression can only reduce redirect-chain I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse or search a page of MCP gallery results
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fetch or read one requested page, parse JSON, validate/convert each server and package, then construct gallery items for display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch one MCP gallery query page
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per explicitly requested page; pagination remains demand-driven.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One network request per page was already made.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The requested page must arrive before its results can display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file read per requested page when the configured gallery uses a file URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same file read path existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read is the page-load boundary for file-backed galleries.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Servers in the requested page and packages/arguments/inputs within each server. Effective parsing remains linear in response size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A page request is serialized by the pager interaction; the diff adds no parallel parsing or boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No page cache was added or removed. Cold and repeated queries each use the existing page boundary.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: serializers and query boundary were inspected across both supported schema families.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual page size and package richness vary, but filtering replaces the prior per-package map and skips unsupported entries rather than adding a second pass.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new package loop has the same linear shape as prior conversion, and schema dispatch avoids speculative full-page fallback work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Map a Copilot NuGet/gallery manifest into a launch configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Parse one fetched manifest, retain supported packages, select the requested package, and construct command arguments before installation/launch can continue.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Package count and argument/environment-variable count in one server manifest; filtering is one linear pass replacing the prior linear map.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous mapping of one manifest; no queue, IPC, filesystem, network, or subprocess operation occurs in the changed mapping functions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates in this pure mapping step and no cache lifecycle changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both serializers, mapping call sites, and command construction were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Manifests may vary in package count, but realistic package arrays are small and the asymptotic work is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Unsupported package types are discarded before command construction; supported mappings do not add boundary work or repeated passes.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 8 changed files and all diff pages. Traced direct installs, deduplicated installed-server synchronization, gallery pagination/parsing, manifest cache behavior, redirect network behavior, and Copilot launch mapping. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
